summary: Feed s111_double to IDS is degraded: 17.6% of TCP sessions are one-way and 13.2% of frames are sliced to 192 bytes, both break IDS state tracking and payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is not aggregating both directions of bidirectional flows to the same IDS tool port. Likely asymmetric routing or hash-based load-balancing/SPAN aggregation is sending client->server and server->client to different outputs, so only one side arrives at s111_double.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP state tracking, stream reassembly and signature correlation. With 24/136 sessions (17.6%) one-way, IDS cannot validate handshakes, misses request/response exploits and generates inaccurate detections.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregating both directions with a bidirectional 5-tuple hash ensures the IDS sees complete sessions for stateful detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker has packet slicing/snaplen enabled truncating frames to ~192 bytes, likely to save bandwidth or fit tool port capacity. 257/1948 frames (13.2%) are cut short.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true) for deep packet inspection and signature matching. Slicing removes application-layer payload, so exploits, malware, and C2 inside truncated packets are invisible to the IDS.

recommended_fix.why: Disabling slicing restores full 1518-byte frames so IDS receives complete L7 payload for detection.
